clue.text: Conscious one isn't in the pink

definitions.text: Conscious one isn't in the pink

parts.words: Conscious one isn't in the pink
parts.note: to be conscious is to sense something, and not being in the pink means being unwell, so this is someone aware of their own poor health

explanation.surface: Someone is aware that they are not in the best of health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conscious' stands for a verb of sensing, and 'in the pink' is an idiom for being in good health, so the whole clue describes someone sensing that they are a little unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aware that you are slightly ill, not in rude health, is the idiom about sensing your own poor colour.

clue.text: Fictional maybe, but basically true

parts.note: describes a story that is invented in its details but rests on real events underneath

explanation.surface: A story is made up yet true at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basically' does the work: the base, or foundation, of the story is real events.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel or film built on real events is described with this phrase, meaning its basis is reality.

clue.text: Sober geezer once-until he reformed

parts.note: describes the joyless old miser of Dickens's A Christmas Carol, who changes his ways after the ghosts visit him

explanation.surface: An old fellow was dour and tight until he changed his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Geezer' is British slang for an old man; the Dickens character of A Christmas Carol was a grim, sober miser until his Christmas Eve visions reformed him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dickens miser was a cheerless old man who mended his ways at the end of the story.

clue.text: Gets stuck up and self, complacent

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: gums means sticks with glue, gets stuck

explanation.surface: Someone is self-satisfied and stuck-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GUMS round. 'stuck up' looks like one idiom for snootiness, but 'up' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-complacent means pleased with oneself, a synonym of self-satisfied.

clue.text: Substitute 1 across, that's in the end, French

parts.note: the 1 across entry says one feels off colour, that is ill
taken as written, placed at the end

explanation.surface: A stand-in for a sick player, a Frenchman, comes in at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 across' refers to the 1-across entry, whose sense, off colour, gives ILL; 'in the end' puts IN last, and French gives F at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A fill-in is a stand-in or temporary replacement for someone.

clue.text: Tom's each move may be traced back to it

definitions.text: Tom's each move may be traced back to it

parts.words: Tom's each move may be traced back to it
parts.note: a tom is a male cat, and his every outing starts from and returns to the place where he lives

explanation.surface: A man called Tom's every movement can be tracked back to a source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name but is a male cat; his base is the house he lives in.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomcat's residence is where every ramble starts and ends.

clue.text: Willowy beauty with a faraway look?

parts.note: willowy means tall and slender, long
a vision is a beautiful person

explanation.surface: A tall, slim beauty gazes into the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Long vision is the ability to see far off, foresight; the question mark marks the literal reading of a faraway look.

clue.text: Evidently not above-board

parts.note: something not above the board sits beneath the shop counter, and things sold there are illicit

explanation.surface: Something is clearly not honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Above-board' means honest, but read literally it means on top of the board, so the opposite is goods kept beneath the counter, sold secretly.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold secretly or illegally are said to come from beneath the shop's counter.

clue.text: One scent-spray for a six-footer, perhaps

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a spray scatters the letters of the word scent into a new order

explanation.surface: A man of six feet tall gets one squirt of perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spray' rearranges SCENT to NSECT. 'six-footer' looks like a tall person but is a creature with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects have six legs, so one is a creature with six feet; 'perhaps' because not every six-legged thing qualifies.

clue.text: Isn't just being different

definitions.meaning: not the same in size or amount

explanation.surface: Someone is unfair for merely being unlike others.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both unfair, as in an uneven contest, and not the same, as in mismatched sizes.

clue.text: Got the picture right on television

definitions.text: Got the picture right on television

parts.words: Got the picture right on television
parts.note: to have the right channel selected on a set, and also to understand, to get the picture

explanation.surface: Someone adjusted the TV set to receive the picture properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got the picture' is also an idiom for understanding, which the phrase means too.
explanation.definitionFit: Set to the correct channel or frequency, and figuratively alert and well-informed.

clue.text: Food prescribed for parliament

definitions.meaning: a regimen of food ordered by a doctor
a legislative assembly, as in some European countries

explanation.surface: Meals are ordered by a doctor for the legislature.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a controlled eating regimen and a formal assembly such as the Japanese legislature.

clue.text: Illuminating contribution from a linesman

parts.note: illuminating suggests lamp, and a linesman is a writer of lines, a poet, producing playful rhymes

explanation.surface: A sports official or electrical worker makes a helpful point.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'linesman' looks like a football official or a utility worker, but here it is a poet who writes lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorous or whimsical poetry is the sort of work a poet produces in a lighter mood.

clue.text: Peak period for high divers?

parts.note: high divers spring off the board, and the season after winter is named for springing

explanation.surface: The best season for those who dive from heights.
explanation.walkthrough: Divers spring from the board, and the season shares the word 'spring'.
explanation.definitionFit: The season between winter and summer, read as the time for springing.

clue.text: Note lamentably piped before a Channel port

indicators.note: played lamentably, the word piped is mangled into a new order

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone played a note badly on the bagpipes before a ferry harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lamentably' is the anagram signal, suggesting bagpipes played badly; the note goes last although the clue names it first. The Channel is the English Channel between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieppe is a French ferry harbour on the coast facing England.

clue.text: It's said to make a terrific impact. Good show!

definitions.text: It's said to make a terrific impact
definitions.meaning: a forceful blow that lands hard
a theatrical production that is a huge success

explanation.surface: A big crash makes a big impression; well done!
explanation.definitionFit: A hugely successful show or record, and literally a violent blow.

clue.text: Feeling more energetic

parts.note: a comparative: having more vigour or power than before

explanation.surface: Someone feels livelier than before.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of powerful or robust describes someone with more vigour.

clue.text: Walking the highway, so to speak

definitions.text: Walking the highway, so to speak

parts.words: Walking the highway, so to speak
parts.note: walking high up, on long poles that raise the walker above the ground

explanation.surface: Someone travels along the main road on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highway' is read as a high way of walking, raised on poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking raised up on long poles with footrests, as circus performers do.

clue.text: See 1 down
Agree to examine a mongrel

parts.note: to con is to study or examine carefully
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to inspect a stray dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to share the same opinion, to be of one mind.

clue.text: Rex on the way out means to go back again

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, king
an egress is an exit

explanation.surface: A king on his way out means to return.
explanation.walkthrough: R for Rex (Latin king) appears in royal signatures such as GR.
explanation.definitionFit: To regress is to revert to an earlier state, to return backwards.

clue.text: Not accustomed to something new

explanation.surface: Someone isn't used to novelty.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both unfamiliar with something and in pristine, never-handled condition.

clue.text: Anything but soft going, of course

definitions.text: Anything but soft going, of course

parts.words: Anything but soft going, of course
parts.note: in horse racing the going is the condition of the course, and the opposite of soft is hard and solid

explanation.surface: Things are not easy, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going' is the racing term for the state of the turf, and 'of course' is a racecourse, not 'naturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid, hard turf is the opposite of soft racing conditions.

clue.text: Noted tea-time fare to fill the gap

parts.note: a bun is a small sweet cake eaten at tea
given a note: G is a musical note added on

explanation.surface: A notable snack at teatime keeps hunger at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means the bun has a note added, G. 'Tea-time' is the British afternoon meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bung is to stop up a hole, as with a cork or plug.

clue.text: A help to advancement in the press

definitions.meaning: a shove or boost that moves something forward
to press is to apply force

explanation.surface: Something that helps one get ahead appears in the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a boost forward in one's career and to press or shove.

clue.text: Grappling with a number facing defeat

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral one hundred
losing means heading for defeat

explanation.surface: A wrestler who is up against a numbered opponent is about to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: To close with an enemy is to come to grips with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing with an opponent means coming to grips, engaging hand to hand.

clue.text: Sacrifice to Davy Jones locker

parts.note: Davy Jones's locker is sailors' slang for the bottom of the sea, so this is deliberately sending a vessel to the seabed

explanation.surface: Something is offered up to the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Davy Jones's locker is the sailors' name for the seabed; deliberately holing a ship to sink it gives it up to the depths.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink one's own ship on purpose, by holing it, is to send it to the seabed.

clue.text: Investments in which there is no immediate interest

definitions.text: Investments in which there is no immediate interest

parts.words: Investments in which there is no immediate interest
parts.note: stock that pays no dividend until a later date or condition, so no return for now

explanation.surface: Some investments hold nobody's attention right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' looks like attention but is the financial return.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock whose holders receive dividends only after others are paid or after a fixed date.
